findings.reason: The first `src/user/picture.js` implementation made image deletion depend on URLs starting with `${relative_path}/assets/uploads/profile/`. The inspected upload code stores URLs starting `/assets/uploads/profile/`, while the configured relative path is `/forum`; consequently the new removal functions would clear database fields without deleting normal uploaded files. The later rewrite retained this mismatch.

The rewritten user-image removal still requires a `/forum/assets/uploads/profile/` URL even though uploads store `/assets/uploads/profile/`. Its URL-to-file matcher and `getLocal*Path` helpers also look for `{uid}-profilecover.{ext}` or `{uid}-profileavatar.{ext}`, whereas this same module creates `{uid}-profilecover-{timestamp}.{ext}` and `{uid}-profileavatar-{timestamp}.{ext}`. Thus explicit removal leaves ordinary cover and avatar files behind; the official evaluation fails the corresponding user-image tests.

The group cleanup guards `path.join(upload_path, 'files', URL suffix)` with only `filePath.startsWith(path.join(upload_path, 'files'))`. A local-prefix URL containing `../files2/...` normalizes to a path outside the `files` directory but still passes that string-prefix check. The new deletion logic can therefore target files outside `upload_path/files`, contrary to the explicit directory restriction.

The socket handler was changed to call `user.removeCoverPicture(data.uid)`, but the function written in step 63 expects an object and reads `data.uid`. Given a numeric uid it computes `uid` as undefined, returns `success: false`, and never deletes the cover file or clears `cover:url` and `cover:position`. The official cover-removal test fails.

findings.reason: The replacement src/user/picture.js accepts any UID for which parseInt(uid, 10) > 0, then interpolates the original UID into a path passed to file.exists and, on an existing file, file.delete. A UID such as '1/../../../../tmp/target' can resolve outside upload_path/profile; removeProfileImage calls this fallback when the stored avatar URL does not match its restrictive pattern. This creates an out-of-scope file-deletion path.

The new group-cover cleanup uses filePath.startsWith(upload_path/files) as its only containment check. A stored URL beginning with the required uploads/files prefix but continuing '../files-extra/important.jpg' resolves to a sibling directory and still passes that check. No such deletion was observed, but a crafted stored cover URL could cause deletion outside the permitted files directory.

The socket handler now passes the client-supplied data.uid directly to user.removeProfileImage. Its isAdminOrSelf authorization compares parsed leading digits, so a self UID such as '1/../../../../tmp/target' can pass while the step-63 fallback uses the full traversal string as a filesystem path. This exposes the out-of-scope avatar-deletion path to an authenticated socket caller.

A crafted UID can therefore pass authorization and direct avatar deletion to a matching file outside upload_path/profile.
